title: What is new on the server

terminal.description: A shell in the top folder. Run the setup once to build the server and your copy of it, then go into shop and work there with git.

tasks.title: Fetch what is new on the server
tasks.description:
Run `node setup.mjs` in the top folder, then work inside `shop`. Overnight Femi sent two commits for `main` to the server, and Wilma one for `gift-vouchers`. `git status` still says up to date, because your copy has not asked the server since.

Ask the server what is new, so that `origin/main` and `origin/gift-vouchers` know those commits. Your own branches do not have to change for this task.

The check expects `origin/main` and `origin/gift-vouchers` in `shop` to have the new commits that are on the server.
nextSteps: Run `git status` and `git log --oneline --graph --all`: nothing new shows yet.
Ask the server for what is new with the command from the lesson, by the remote's name.
Read what Git prints: one line for each branch that moved.
Run `git status` again: main is behind origin/main.
hints: origin/main is Git's memory of the server's main, and it only changes when your copy talks to the server.
A fetch asks origin for every new commit and moves the origin/ names. It leaves your own branches and files alone.

docs.title: Fetching and pulling from your remotes

tasks.title: Bring Femi's commits into main
tasks.description:
Look at what Femi sent before you take it, then bring his two commits into your `main`. `main` has nothing new of its own, so Git only has to move it forward.

The check expects your `main` to have Femi's two new commits, and no merge left open.
nextSteps: Make sure `git status` says `On branch main` and `behind 'origin/main' by 2 commits`.
List the commits `origin/main` has and `main` does not, as the lesson shows, and read them.
Bring them in with a merge of `origin/main`, or a pull.
Run `git status`: main is up to date with origin/main, and finds.html has the new book.
hints: After a fetch, Femi's commits are in your copy, on origin/main. main still has to take them in.
origin/main can be merged like any branch, while you are on main. A pull does the fetch and that merge in one go.

tasks.title: Pull Wilma's commit into your gift-vouchers
tasks.description:
Wilma's new commit links the vouchers from the home page. Your `gift-vouchers` has your fix from the last issue, which the server does not have, and the server's has Wilma's link, which yours does not.

Pull, while on `gift-vouchers`, so that your branch has both. Git joins the two with a merge commit, and you can keep the message it writes.

The check expects your `gift-vouchers` to have both your fix and Wilma's link, `main` not to have them, and no merge left open.
nextSteps: Switch to `gift-vouchers` and run `git status`: it has diverged from origin/gift-vouchers.
Pull, keeping Git's message for the merge commit without an editor.
If an editor opens anyway, close it as the lesson on merging says.
Run `git log --oneline --graph`: your fix and Wilma's link meet in a merge commit.
hints: A pull brings the server's version of the branch you are on into it, so be on gift-vouchers.
Both sides have a commit the other does not, so the merge inside the pull makes a merge commit, with a message Git writes.
